b: Salivary duct stones (sialolithiasis): commoner in the submandibular gland (about 80%, because of its long, uphill duct and viscous mucus) than the parotid. Pain and swelling of the gland on eating (meal-time syndrome) ; a stone may be felt

Sialadenitis: acute infection of the parotid or submandibular gland in the elderly, dehydrated or immunocompromised ; treat with hydration, antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate or clindamycin), sialogogues, massage ; ultrasound excludes an
Benign tumours: about 80% of salivary tumours occur in the parotid , and about 80% of those are benign .

Pleomorphic adenoma (the commonest, about 80% of benign tumours): a slow-growing, painless, mobile lump with no skin changes, usually in the superficial lobe. About 5% undergo malignant transformation (carcinoma ex-pleomorphic adenoma) and
Warthin's tumour (papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum): second commonest; older male smokers , may be bilateral , cystic; malignant change about 0.3%.
